questions.question: Government of India Act of 1935 had ___________ schedules.
questions.solution:
The Government of India Act of 1935 was a major step towards a federal form of government.
  • It contained 321 sections and 10 schedules.
  • It abolished Dyarchy in provinces and introduced it at the Center.

questions.question: The Gopatha Brahmana is related to which of the following Vedas?
questions.solution:
The Gopatha Brahmana is the only Brahmana text associated with the Atharvaveda.
  • Brahmanas are prose texts that explain the hymns of the Vedas and ritual instructions.
  • Atharvaveda deals with magic, spells, and daily life.

questions.question: Who founded the Kanva dynasty after the death of the last Shunga ruler?
questions.solution:
The Kanva dynasty was founded by Vasudeva Kanva in 73 BCE.
  • He overthrew Devabhuti, the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty.
  • The dynasty ruled from Magadha for a short period.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Prarthana Samaj, which promoted social reform in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The Prarthana Samaj was founded by Atmaram Pandurang in 1867 in Bombay.
  • It was inspired by the Brahmo Samaj and worked for social reforms like widow remarriage and abolition of caste.
  • Prominent leaders included M.G. Ranade.

questions.question: During the 1930s, Lord Zetland played a significant role in which of the following events related to India's constitutional reforms?
questions.solution:
Lord Zetland was the Secretary of State for India during the Round Table Conferences in London.
  • These conferences were held between 1930-1932 to discuss constitutional reforms in India based on the Simon Commission report.

questions.question: Which ruler of Haryanka Dynasty annexed several important and powerful kingdoms in its vicinity such as Kosala, Kashi and Vajji?
questions.solution:
Ajatashatru was a powerful ruler of the Haryanka Dynasty who expanded the Magadha Empire.
  • He conquered Vajji (Vaishali) and Kosala.
  • He was the son of Bimbisara and convened the First Buddhist Council.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is NOT mentioned in Rigveda?
questions.solution:
The Rigveda mentions various rivers like the Saraswati, Sindhu (Indus), and Yamuna, but Krishna is not mentioned as it is located in Southern India.
  • Saraswati is considered the most sacred river in the Rigveda.

questions.question: Who among the following authored the book ‘Sarvajanik Satyadharma’?
questions.solution:
Jyotiba Phule authored Sarvajanik Satyadharma and Gulamgiri.
  • He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to fight for the rights of lower castes and women.

questions.question: Who led the Aligarh Movement to modernise education for Muslims in India?
questions.solution:
The Aligarh Movement was led by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan.
  • He founded the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College in 1875, which later became Aligarh Muslim University (AMU).
  • It aimed at promoting modern education among Muslims.

questions.question: According to a Buddhist text, how many oligarchic republics or kingdoms, called Mahajanapadas, ruled ancient India during the 6th to 4th centuries BCE?
questions.solution:
Buddhist texts like Anguttara Nikaya mention the existence of 16 Mahajanapadas (large kingdoms/republics).
  • Prominent ones included Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, and Avanti.

questions.question: Which king of the Maukharis claimed to have defeated the Later Guptas?
questions.solution:
Sarvavarman was a significant ruler of the Maukhari dynasty of Kannauj.
  • He expanded his kingdom and successfully challenged the Later Guptas, establishing Maukhari dominance in North India.

questions.question: In which year was the Cripps Mission sent to India?
questions.solution:
The Cripps Mission was sent to India in 1942 under Sir Stafford Cripps.
  • It aimed to secure Indian cooperation for World War II.
  • Gandhiji called it a 'Post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'.

questions.question: In which of the following Buddhist texts are the rules mentioned for Buddhist monks and nuns?
questions.solution:
The Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules and regulations for Buddhist monks and nuns (the Sangha).
  • The Sutta Pitaka contains Buddha's teachings, and Abhidhamma Pitaka deals with philosophy.

questions.question: Which women's organisation was founded by Sarojini Naidu in 1917?
questions.solution:
The Women's India Association (WIA) was founded in 1917 at Adyar, Madras.
  • Sarojini Naidu, Annie Besant, and Margaret Cousins were key figures.
  • It fought for women's suffrage and education.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was started by Pandita Ramabai Saraswati in 1882?
questions.solution:
Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj in 1882 in Pune.
  • She also established Sharada Sadan for the education of young widows.
  • She was a pioneer in women's rights and medical education.

questions.question: Which of the following periods does the Iron Age in India encompass?
questions.solution:
The Iron Age in the Indian subcontinent is generally dated between 1500 BCE and 200 BCE.
  • It is associated with the Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture in Northern India.

questions.question: The Indian Association, founded in 1876, was established by:
questions.option_1: Lala Lajpat Rai and Chittaranjan Das
questions.option_4: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pa
questions.solution:
The Indian Association (1876) was the first avowed nationalist organization founded in British India.
  • Founders: Surendranath Banerjee and Anandamohan Bose.
  • It later merged with the Indian National Congress.

questions.question: Which dynasty succeeded the Mauryan Empire?
questions.solution:
The Shunga dynasty succeeded the Mauryan Empire in 185 BCE.
  • Pushyamitra Shunga, the commander-in-chief, assassinated the last Mauryan king.

questions.question: Generally, what portion of the crop was collected as tax by the state during the Mahajanapada period?
questions.solution:
During the Mahajanapada period, the state usually collected 1/6th of the agricultural produce as tax.
  • This tax was known as 'Bhaga' (share).

questions.question: The Partition of Bengal was implemented by which British official?
questions.solution:
The Partition of Bengal was implemented by Lord Curzon in 1905.
  • It led to the Swadeshi Movement. The partition was eventually annulled in 1911.

questions.question: Which title did the Maukharis adopt to imitate the earlier Guptas?
questions.solution:
To assert their sovereignty and imitate the Imperial Guptas, the Maukharis adopted the title of Maharajadhiraja.
  • This title means 'King of Kings'.

questions.question: In which year was the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) established?
questions.solution:
The All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) was established in 1920.
  • Its first session was held in Bombay with Lala Lajpat Rai as its president.

questions.question: Which Greek ambassador chronicled his observations during his visit to the court of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
Megasthenes was the Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
  • He wrote the book 'Indica', which describes Mauryan administration and society.

questions.question: Which movement was launched in 1942 with the call for 'Do or Die'?
questions.solution:
The Quit India Movement was launched in August 1942.
  • Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous slogan 'Do or Die' (Karo Ya Maro) at the Gowalia Tank Maidan.

questions.question: The three-age system for classification of pre-historic periods was introduced by:
questions.solution: The Three-age system (Stone, Bronze, and Iron Age) was developed by the Danish archaeologist Christian Jurgensen Thomsen in the early 19th century.
